title: Compact Context Store and Session Proxy API Sketch
content:
PURPOSE
------
Quick sketch for a compact on-client context store API and a lightweight session proxy contract. Goal: enable client devices (mobile/web) to hold a small, efficiently-serialized prefix/embedding cache and to sync deltas with Redwood session proxies for retrieval-aware routing. This is a personal draft — rough, intentionally terse.

BACKGROUND
----------
We want to reduce token-by-token cost and latencies by allowing clients to cache recent conversation context and embeddings. The server-side runtime already supports KV caching per request; this sketches a complementary client-side compact store and a tiny session proxy that mediates what gets pinned to the long-running serving KV cache.

KEY DESIGN CONSTRAINTS
----------------------
- Compact on-disk memory: goal ~= <50KB per active session for small devices.
- Streamable / append-friendly format so partial writes are resilient.
- Delta sync only: avoid full snapshot transfers after initial handshake.
- Server should be able to request/subscribe to specific keys (e.g., user mentions) for retrieval.
- Forward-compatible: schema versioning in header.

CORE CONCEPTS
-------------
- Snapshot: full serialized representation of session context (rarely transmitted).
- DeltaPatch: small ops (append-token, truncate, tag, pin, unpin).
- CompactKey: opaque identifier referencing cached prefix segments or embedding blobs.
- SessionProxy: ephemeral server-side component that accepts deltas, validates them, and offers retrieval and pinning operations to the serving runtime.

ASCII FLOW
---------
Client                          SessionProxy                          ServingRuntime
  | -------- handshake --------> |                                      |
  | <-- session-id, ver, ttl --- |                                      |
  | -- deltaPatch(upload) --->   | -- enqueue for merge / validate --> |
  | <--- ack / conflict -------- | <--- maybe request snapshot ------- |
  | -- pinRequest(key) ------->  | -- pin to runtime ----------------> |
  | <--- pinAck ---------------  | <--- ok --------------------------- |

API SKETCHES (HTTP/json)
------------------------
Base path: /v1/client-sessions/{session_id}/compact
Auth: session token (short-lived) + device signature header (TBD)

1) Handshake / register client copy
POST /v1/client-sessions/{session_id}/compact/handshake\Body: {
  "client_id": "str",
  "client_schema_version": "1",
  "capabilities": ["delta-only","snapshots","embeddings"],
  "last_known_seq": "int"
}
Response: { "session_id": "str", "server_schema_version": "1", "assigned_client_rev": "int", "retry_after": 0 }

Purpose: align sequence numbers and schema; server may respond with request for full snapshot if client is stale.

2) Upload delta patch
POST /v1/client-sessions/{session_id}/compact/delta\Body: {
  "seq": 123,
  "base_seq": 120,            // server seq this patch is built on
  "ops": [                   // small set of ops (ordered)
     {"op":"append_tokens","tokens":"...","meta":{"role":"user"}},
     {"op":"pin","key":"ctx:seg:20260309:abcd","ttl_secs":86400},
     {"op":"embed_update","key":"emb:seg:abcd","vector_len":768,"data":"base64..."}
  ],
  "ttl_secs": 86400,
  "client_ts": "2026-03-09T12:34:56Z"
}
Response: {"ack_seq": 123, "merged_seq": 125, "conflict": false, "server_requests_snapshot": false}

Notes: ops must be idempotent by seq. Server returns merged_seq (internal sequence after applying other concurrent patches) to help client realign. If conflict=true, server will ask for snapshot or diff-manual resolution.

3) Request full snapshot
GET /v1/client-sessions/{session_id}/compact/snapshot?format=compact\Response: content-type: application/octet-stream (proprietary compact format) or JSON for debug.

4) Pin request (explicit) -- faster path for small pins
POST /v1/client-sessions/{session_id}/compact/pin\Body: {"key":"ctx:seg:20260309:abcd","source":"client","priority":"high","ttl_secs":3600}
Response: {"pinned": true, "pin_id":"pin-abc-123", "runtime_placement": "dedicated-gpu-3"}

SCHEMA: COMPACT SNAPSHOT (textual)
---------------------------------
Header (plaintext JSON, small): {"schema":1, "seq":125, "created":"2026-03-09T12:00:00Z", "compressed":true}
Followed by: zlib compressed binary payload. Contents (after decompress): ND json lines or small binary TLV of segments. Example decompressed body (human-readable):
[
  {"key":"ctx:seg:1","start_token":0,"end_token":120,"type":"text","compressed":true},
  {"key":"emb:seg:1","vector_len":768,"count":2}
]

DeltaPatch op vocabulary (constrained and intentionally small)
- append_tokens {tokens, meta}
- truncate_prefix {tokens_to_drop}
- pin {key, ttl_secs, priority}
- unpin {key}
- embed_update {key, data_base64, method:"avg|first|last"}
- annotate {key, tags:[...]}

EVICTION / PRUNING CONFIG (client local; declarative)
{"evict_policy":"LRU|time|length_based", "max_size_bytes": 51200, "min_retention_secs": 3600, "pin_protection": true}
Notes: client will always respect server pin/unpin instructions when present.

PROXY BEHAVIOR: VALIDATION & RATE GUARDS
---------------------------------------
- Validate seq monotonicity, reject older seqs with error code 409 and include server current seq.
- Small ops (<4KB) are accepted inline; larger blobs (embeddings) must be uploaded via signed multipart to blob-store; proxy will return upload_url on 413-like response.
- Proxy may ask server to materialize pin into runtime (async) and will surface placement to client for observability.

EXAMPLE: CLIENT -> DELTAPATCH with EMBED BLOB\\nRequest body (truncated): {"seq": 128, "ops":[{"op":"embed_update","key":"emb:seg:abcd","vector_len":768,"blob_ref":"s3://redwood-compact/emb/abcd"}]}
Server response: {"ack_seq":128, "merged_seq":129, "blob_received":false, "upload_url":"https://uploads.rdl..."}

CONFLICT RESOLUTION STRATEGY
----------------------------
- Best-effort merge for append_tokens and embed_update (embeds replace by key).
- If incompatible ops (e.g., different truncates on same range), return conflict with minimal instructions: {"action":"request_snapshot"} or {"action":"manual_merge","server_hint":"rebase_to_seq:125"}.

OBSERVABILITY / METRICS
-----------------------
- Per-session metrics: last_seq_applied, pending_deltas, avg_delta_size, pin_count.
- Events: client_snapshot_requested, conflict_detected, blob_upload_failed.

SECURITY THOUGHTS
-----------------
- Client uploads must be signed; sessions are short-lived and tied to device.
- Embedding blobs may be encrypted with per-customer KMS key before storing in shared blob store.
- Rate-limit by session_id + client_id to mitigate noisy clients.

OPEN QUESTIONS
--------------
- Should embed blobs be chunked or kept as single unit? (trade-off: single blob easier but larger than 50KB cap)
- How aggressively do we accept client-side pin requests vs server-initiated pins? Need policy for untrusted clients.
- Offline-first: how to rehydrate huge snapshots on low-bandwidth devices? Possibly tiered snapshots (summary + missing detail on demand).
- Server-side TTL interplay with client TTL: which wins when they differ? Propose server is authoritative.

NEXT STEPS / ACTIONS
--------------------
- Prototype compact binary layout (TLV) and zlib wrapper (Ethan)
- Implement minimal proxy handlers for handshake/delta/pin (PoC route) (owner + Maya)
- Add metric hooks and a small conformance test harness (unit tests for monotonic seq, conflict cases)
- Draft a short security note about upload signing and KMS usage

NOTES TO SELF
------------
- Keep op vocabulary small. If we need more semantics later, extend with new op names and bump schema.
- Aim for graceful degradation: if client misbehaves, server should fall back to serving without client cache.

END OF SCRATCHPAD
(This is intentionally rough; will convert to a more formal PRD if the PoC shows viability.)
